bluf: JBH is a founder led Manchester and London digital PR and SEO agency (founded 2013, Jane Hunt as CEO) that sells making mid market consumer brands famous in media and search through links and mentions, and now leads its headline with a GEO claim: that its PR lifted the finance brand Clifton to the top of AI search answers. The record shows a well described book, 14 of 17 clients with an observed need, almost all PR, and productised pricing signals. Horus reads it Favored at 26.4; Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 61.7. What a rival should know: it sells GEO and publishes no llms.txt.
doing:
The positioning line, "Performance-first digital PR and SEO agency with offices in Manchester and London, making consumer brands famous in media and search through links and mentions," decodes to a link and mention machine: coverage that earns links for SEO and mentions for AI answers, sold to consumer brands as performance. The headline claim, that "expert-led PR lifted specialist finance brand Clifton to the top of AI search answers," is quoted as a claim and rests on a single GEO case study dated July 2026.

The sold mix leads with Content & Digital PR, scored 3: the homepage title and H1 brand JBH a digital PR agency. AI Search / GEO and SEO each score 2: a GEO agency page covers entities, prompt mapping and measurement, with the Clifton case; a dedicated SEO page covers on site content, link building and ecommerce SEO, and a Director of SEO sits on the senior team. CRO scores 1; every other line, Data & Measurement and all paid media included, scores 0, so breadth is 4. The services list runs Digital PR, Traditional PR, SEO, GEO, CRO, a reactive PR and newsjacking press office, and sector lines for beauty, personal finance and healthcare PR. Proprietary lines: the Digital PR Playbook and the PR Percentage Calculator; no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is GEO built on brand mentions, digital PR, NLP and prompt mapping to win visibility in ChatGPT, AI Mode, Gemini and Claude; no audited AI visibility product shows (P1 partial).

The only dated move is a 2022 award, PR Agency of the Year, awarding body not named; the record lists no news and no job posting. Pricing signals are present: the digital PR page is headed around guaranteed links and digital PR packages, implying productised pricing, though no rates are seen (P5 making). Absent for a performance first agency: any measurement line, a headcount, and a dated move since 2022.
clients:
The ICP is mid market; the home market is the UK, with Manchester and London listed. Verticals on record: personal finance, beauty, healthcare, consumer retail and ecommerce, car leasing, language learning, divorce mediation, drinks and price comparison.

The record names 17 clients through case studies, and 14 carry an observed need: PR, reputation and content dominates with 13 of 17 (a 0.894 share). Clifton came for AI visibility, the signal being the GEO case study category (N9). The PR signals are digital PR outreach case studies: Uswitch (the TV shows that get the most complaints), Preply, Equitable Mediation, Workwear Express, Delamere Health, Radar Healthcare and The Bottle Club, plus Cosmetify, whose beauty campaign is also coded brand and creative (N12, N3). Sector service pages supply the rest: Better.co.uk and money.co.uk under personal finance PR, Spacegoods and HD Brows, Nouveau Lashes & KB Pro under beauty PR, and Resound under the healthcare page. Select Car Leasing, The Neem Tree and Your Baby Club are coded N0, names only, their need inferred from the sold mix as PR.

The shared count is 2: Preply also sits on the kaizen and junto books, and Uswitch on aira.

What the base needs next, tied to the edition: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is the read's best placement, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, so these finance, beauty and healthcare brands will very likely ask for the Clifton result repeated and measured, which the record shows on the GEO page but not as an audited product (moderate confidence). KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) is its exposure on SEO, so clients who bought links for rankings likely ask what the links now prove.
house: Say and do: AI Search / GEO is contradicted, since it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while its sitemap holds 5 AI topic URLs, the one gap the Radar flagged; no AI crawlers are listed as blocked. Publishing cadence is corroborated: 3 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 16 in 365, from 235 URLs. Say/do integrity is 50. The Transparency Center shows 2 Google text ads under JACKSON BLASON HUNT LTD, 0 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-02-12, so its own paid presence has lapsed; no sample is recorded. LinkedIn shows 0 ads, with 0 matching the name query. The tag stack is empty in the record, on WordPress: no tag manager, no social pixels, no test tools and no ABM stack, which is thin for a house that sells CRO and calls itself performance first. Meta and TikTok status is not recorded.

Horus reads JBH at a tailwind index of 26.4, band Favored, 16:57 on the Solar Arc, dusk, say/do integrity 50. Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), net 0.547, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR. Monsoon reads 61.7, band Onshore wind: migration 61.7 and displacement 61.7. The sold mix supplies 62 of the index, SEO (22) and Content & Digital PR (21) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia, 20% to Eastern Europe and 15% to Africa and the Maghreb. openings:
The strongest opening is the say/do gap on GEO: it leads its headline with lifting Clifton to the top of AI answers and sells prompt mapping and measurement, yet publishes no llms.txt and shows no audited citation share or scorecard product (P1 partial), so a rival with an audited AI visibility number and its own llms.txt very likely wins the finance or beauty buyer who asks for the Clifton result on their own brand (high confidence on the gap, moderate on the win). The falsifier: an llms.txt on jbh.co.uk or a named AI visibility scorecard at the next compile.

Second, measurement: KJ9 is its exposure, Data & Measurement scores 0 and the tag stack is empty, so a rival that shows what links and mentions prove likely holds the SEO line against it.

Third, the lapsed house: its own Google ads were last shown 2026-02-12 and LinkedIn shows 0, so a rival very likely owns the paid conversation around digital PR packages. On price, displacement reads 61.7, so an offshore delivered rival has roughly an even chance of undercutting its guaranteed link packages, though its productised pricing lets it answer in public. Preply and Uswitch already shop.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind that its GEO headline depends on.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would strengthen KJ8, its second tailwind, on human made digital PR.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and any pricing below $20 CPM would signal supply outrunning demand under KJ2.

The July 2026 Clifton GEO case study is the dated item to follow up, and the next Radar compile (the dossier is only as fresh as 2026-09-28) should show whether a second GEO case, an llms.txt or a renewed Google ad appears after the 2026-02-12 last shown date.
